lina.marketing: Quick final-pass please  battlecard + 3 micro-scripts for launch email. Need lines that contrast Redwood vs cloud platforms, LLM APIs, infra vendors.
own.ae: For AEs: focus on cost predictability, rollout controls, and verified latency under load. Short bullets.
marc.prod: Callout: mention p95 target (<=300ms) and 'model-variant fallbacks' as ops feature.
tasha.design: I'll keep layout modular: hero, 3 competitor buckets, 3 quick rebuttals, footer with bench note.
ivy.data: Bench snapshot (internal): public_api p50=205ms p95=540ms; redwood_dedicated p50=92ms p95=260ms; cost example public $0.026/1k vs dedicated $0.012/1k. Do not publish raw numbers.
copy-bot: Draft hero: "Serving-first inference  predictable latency, transparent unit economics, rollout controls."
own.ae: AE micro-scripts (email subject + one-liner): 1) Subject: "Avoid surprise inference costs" Body: "We help teams reduce per-token spend and keep demo latency stable under real traffic." 2) Subject: "Keep SLAs during bursts" Body: "Smart routing + model fallbacks preserve UX when regions get hot." 3) Subject: "Ship rollouts confidently" Body: "Canary/A-B with automatic fallback means safer rollouts without ops churn."
marc.prod: Rebuttal bullets vs buckets: Cloud platforms: "Convenient but variable economics and regional throttling." LLM APIs: "Fast iteration; limited rollout controls and opaque unit costs." Infra vendors: "Control but long setup and high maintenance tax."
lina.marketing: Footer bench line for webinar slide: "Method: replayed 10k real requests; cache & batching enabled; measured p50/p95 and normalized cost/1k tokens. Numbers vary by workload."
ivy.data: Note: legal wants qualifiers like 'up to' and 'typical' on cost claims.
copy-bot: Action items: tasha to deliver one-pager mock by EOD, lina to run legal check, owen to prep AE deck, marc to finalize demo p95 scripts. Lock copy tomorrow AM. :tada:
